newsitem.title: USA: U.S. net written premiums seen up 3.1 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. net written premiums seen up 3.1 pct in 1997.

text.p: U.S. net written premiums are expected to grow 3.1 percent in 1997, just slightly faster than the estimated increase of 3.0 percent in 1996, according to a U.S. insurance industry survey.
In its annual Groundhog Day survey, the Insurance Information Institute asks stock analysts to forecast the outlook for the U.S. property-casualty industry.
In the 1997 Groundhog forecast, analysts also projected a combined ratio after dividends of 107.0 percent, up from the estimated 106.1 percent in 1996.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
This year's combined ratio forecast is the gloomiest since 1994, the institute said.

The institute said the projections for the combined ratio showed a much wider variation than normal for 1997, varying from a high of 108 percent by KPMG Peat Marwick to a low of 104.5 percent by Conning & Co.

The institute said this probably reflects increasing uncertainty about two major factors: catastrophes and reserve levels, which have become increasingly difficult to project for the property-casualty insurance business.
The forecasts for net written premium growth ranged from a high of 3.6 percent by Conning & Co and a low of 2.0 percent by Bankers Trust Securities Corp, the institute said.
